scope: Binary datapath primitives used in the Section 5 factoring reduction. On unsigned words that fit in w bits, one 6w-gate ripple subtraction computes a comparison or a saturating predecessor. Fixed-width wiring and branch selection use the repository’s branching-program model.

Computes the gcd of two unsigned w-bit integers by binary restoring division and the Euclidean remainder recurrence. A public limit of 2w divisions suffices and at most 40(w+1)³ Boolean arithmetic gates are charged.

Implements the factoring reduction’s even-number and perfect-power checks. For a b-bit input it tests small exponents by binary root search, carries exact powers in (b+1)² bits, and returns the same optional divisor as the executable preprocessor within 100(b+1)⁶ Boolean arithmetic gates.

Implements the Section 5 gcd reduction and checks both children of a proposed split. Word-based modular powering, Euclidean gcd and one restoring division agree with extractFactor and certify. Every successful pair includes the actual quotient.

Converts a fair binary word into the same positive base as the probability proof, and detects words outside the allowed range. A comparison, decrement and increment cost at most 18w Boolean arithmetic gates.

The decoder returns an order candidate at most the clock size. With a proper positive base and a fitting positive clock, the postprocessing branch returns the certified divisor and cofactor from the same observed clock value within 2000(w+1)⁴ Boolean arithmetic gates. Nonunit bases take the gcd branch directly.

For m ≥ 2, a fair word fitting floor(log₂ m)+1 bits, and a measured record below a clock size fitting twice that width plus two bits, all classical branches of a factor attempt return exactly the verified split and cost at most 10⁶(floor(log₂ m)+2)⁶ Boolean arithmetic gates.

ForShor’s weighted logical-gate count for the allocated order-finding circuit is bounded uniformly over every modulus and legal coprime base by C(floor(log₂ m)+1)³. A finite maximum absorbs the small inputs left open by the asymptotic circuit theorem.
Lifts a bound on one modulus to the actual recursive divisor tree by summing over the nodes the splitter visits. Binary input widths decrease along subproblems.

At every tape for input N, the adaptively visited subproblems, including all bases in a padded batch, cost at most C(floor(log₂ N)+1)⁶ logical gates in the pinned ForShor resource model. This is an execution count for the specified circuit family.

The fair base word and actual Fourier clock fit the argument widths required by the bit-level factoring program. Taking the finite maximum of the program’s costs over the physical records preserves the polynomial one-shot bound.

Connects each branch in the physical law to the bit-level program. On a coprime base it processes the same clock result, a nonunit yields its gcd, an oversized draw is rejected, and successful preprocessing returns the divisor together with its cofactor.

For every recursive tape, with L=floor(log₂ N), the total classical trial datapath cost is at most 768000000(L+2)⁹ Boolean arithmetic gates and at most 768(L+1)⁴ independent fair bits need be drawn for base selection. Both counts pad every visited modulus to a full batch.

Every factor fits in the original binary word and there are at most floor(log₂ m) leaves below a recursive call at m ≥ 2. Even copying the complete output list at each return takes at most 2(floor(log₂ N)+2)³ bit writes under the fixed-width tagged representation.

Shor Sections 3–5 at the level of adaptive logical-circuit execution. For every positive N the physical procedure returns a product equal to N on every tape and a prime factorization with probability at least 2/3. Worst-case bounds jointly cover weighted logical gates, binary trial arithmetic, random bits and output copies. Shor’s Section 2 uniform circuit-construction and numerical gate-entry generation costs are separate.
